english.title: Aid abet a person to threaten with a blade / sharply pointed article on school premises

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Legal Aid Sentencing and punishment of offenders Act 2012

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), had with

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

an article, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ARTICLE..), to which section 139AA of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 applies on school premises, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SCHOOL PREMISES..), and you aided, abetted, counselled or procured

(C)_[him]_
(D)_[her]_

to unlawfully and intentionally threaten another, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON THREATENED..), with that article in such a way that there was an immediate risk of serious physical harm to that person
english.legislation: Contrary to section 139AA(1) and (6) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 and section 8 of the Accessories and Abettors Act 1861.

english.notes:
(i) "Public place" is defined in section 139(7) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988.
(ii) "Article" is defined in section 139(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988.
(iii) "School premises" are defined in section 139A(6) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988.
(iv) The court may find the defendant not guilty of this offence but guilty of an offence under section 139 or 139A of the Act.
(v) Section 139AA was amended to extend the offence to cover not only school premises, but also further education premises and insert an objective element into the offence; for offences committed on or after 6th April 2022 see H20306.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 4 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

For minimum sentence for this offence see section 312 of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
